Two-point photometric calibration cannot rescue this: black from the fiducials and white from the annulus pin the two endpoints, but gamma is a nonlinearity BETWEEN the endpoints, so d = (W - m)/(W - K) is compressed by roughly 1.5x in the low third where the ink floor lives. The design's own claim that f "has a physical meaning: the estimated ink coverage" is off by about 35 percent at 0.30 coverage. Worse, the error is a deterministic bias, not noise: it survives the three-shot rule, the digest comparison, and criteria 8, 12 and 13 unchanged. Tiers 0 through 3 all pass at 100 percent, on both targets, while the phone silently marks answered questions blank. No portability seam in this design is checked for this, and GrayImage carries no field that could describe it.
verdicts.concreteFailure: Executed against the on-disk implementation of this architecture. Render quick20 with one mark on q5, symbol D, coverage 0.9, pencil grey 150 on paper 248 with ink 18. That is not a synthetic edge case: it is verbatim the case the repo's own test/scan.test.ts labels "A hard pencil, shaded through: light, but a real answer" and asserts must return D. Scanning the linear render returns q5 = D, confident, no flag. Applying the transfer function a real sensor applies before Y is written (a 256-entry pow(v/255, 1/2.2) LUT, nothing else changed) and re-scanning the same sheet returns q5 = blank. Arithmetic: inkRatio linear = (248-150)/(248-18) = 0.426, comfortably over minInk 0.25; gamma encoded, paper 248 becomes 251.8, mark 150 becomes 201.7, ink 18 becomes 79.2, so inkRatio = (251.8-201.7)/(251.8-79.2) = 0.290, and after the disc average it lands under the 0.25 floor. I swept the pencil value: 55 and 110 agree on both, 140 turns from D into D-uncertain, 150 and 160 turn from D (and D-uncertain) into blank, so the whole decision band shifts by about one pencil grade. A student writing with an H or 2H pencil gets a blank on every question and the teacher sees only "blanks: 50", which д8 defines as the student's own decision. Second, measured failure, on the same lens: I re-ran the pipeline under V8 with --jitless, an interpreter-only engine and a fair proxy for Hermes, which ships no optimizing JIT in React Native. standard50 at 1440x2560 (the minimum resolution 4ب-7 mandates) costs 372 ms with the perturbation set off and 922 ms with it on, versus 25 ms and 82 ms with the JIT. That is an 11x to 16x penalty on a desktop x86 core, not the 3x to 5x this design assumes when it writes "55 ms in V8, an estimated 150 to 250 ms on Hermes". A mid-range ARM core is 2x to 4x slower again, so the honest first-frame number on Hermes is 0.7 to 3.7 seconds, for one frame, on a 50-question sheet; full100 has 540 bubbles against 294. Rule 3 then wants three of them. And layoutSheet costs 13.5 ms per call in the interpreter because layout/index.ts:47-48 runs encodeSheetCode plus a full QR generation, Reed-Solomon and eight-mask penalty scoring included, on every call; stage 10 calls it once per candidate spec per frame, so a ten-template catalog is 135 ms of thrown-away QR generation before a pixel is read.
verdicts.salvage: Four changes, three of them cheap, one of them fatal to the design's own framing. (1) Put the transfer function in the type. GrayImage grows a transfer field ('linear' | 'gamma22' | 'srgb'), the boundary applies a 256-entry linearisation LUT once (free: 256 pow calls at init, then one array read per sample, and it can be folded into inkRatio), and render.ts emits gamma-encoded output so CI feeds the engine what a phone feeds it. Then add the honest caveat the design cannot avoid: device Y is not one fixed curve (video versus full range varies by Android stream, and iPhone local tone mapping is not a fixed function at all), so a floor that survives it must come from a printed mid-grey reference the sheet does not yet print. Two solid-black targets plus paper white is two points, and a nonlinearity needs three. That is a sheet-spec change, and paper.ts says a sheet-spec change bumps SheetSpec.version, so it is now-or-never in 4ب-3's sense. Critically, none of this is a "calibration constant", so the design's headline promise that the 300 photographs may only move constants and never the algorithm has to be withdrawn: it is exactly the promise that hid this. (2) Budget against a measured interpreter, not an assumed 3x. Add tools/bench.ts run under node --jitless in CI today as the floor, gate it at 400 ms for full100 at 1440p, and hand the app layer a lock-then-track path that is not optional. (3) Add a ScanWorkspace so the integral (Int32Array over the decimated frame, about 3.6 MB at a 700 px short side), the label array (another 3.6 MB) and the mask are allocated once and reused, and cache layoutSheet and bubbleGroups per templateId across frames. Nothing in the 20-file layout does either today, and PLAN rule 4 is explicit that frame-loop memory discipline is not optional. (4) Delete the platform-barcode-API punt and write the QR decoder in TypeScript. The design's one cross-target divergence is at the step that carries the whole geometry, and it is the step CI cannot test (the DEVLOG records BarcodeDetector as unavailable on headless Linux), so the self-describing path, the product's actual differentiator, would be the only path the golden set never certifies. The repo already proves the punt was unnecessary: src/qr/ is eight files and about 800 lines, zero dependencies, with tests. Two smaller items: GrayImage also needs pixelStride and a plane byte offset, because Android's Image.Plane permits Y pixelStride greater than 1 and VisionCamera hands back the whole native buffer, and the design's only validation (data.length >= rowStride*height) accepts a 2-stride plane and reads a horizontally halved image that the [0.66, 1.5] aspect gate then rejects as "no sheet" with no cause, which 4ب-1 names as the highest-traffic support topic in the category. And MIN_PX_PER_MM 3.0 contradicts д11, which requires 3 px per 0.5 mm module, that is 6 px/mm; the gate as written admits frames at half the density the defense demands.
verdicts.verdict: The architecture is right and the arithmetic under it is wrong. Rejecting OpenCV, rejecting WASM (Hermes has none), rejecting the injected CvBackend seam, and deleting the warp in favour of forward millimetre sampling are all correct, and I can now say "correct" rather than "plausible" because an implementation of this same shape is sitting uncommitted in packages/core-omr/src and I ran it: 25 to 37 ms per sheet in V8, nearly flat from 3.7 to 12.2 MP, honouring rowStride, no native handle anywhere near scanSheet. Graft that. But the design mistakes a compute budget for a portability argument. It never asks what the bytes in the Y plane MEAN, and the answer is the one thing that differs between its two targets: CI gets linear coverage from a rasteriser the authors wrote, the phone gets gamma-encoded video-range luma from a sensor pipeline they do not control, and every absolute threshold in the package is calibrated on the first. A hard-pencil mark at grey 150, the repo's own definition of "light, but a real answer", reads D in CI and blank on a gamma-encoded frame, deterministically, through all three shots and through the perturbation set, so criteria 8, 12 and 13 certify it and criterion 11 fails only on real paper. Its five named risks include specular glare, rolling shutter, JPEG ringing and graphite texture, and not the transfer function, which is the one that actually flips a grade. The performance case is off by a smaller but still disqualifying factor: 11x to 16x measured for an interpreter versus JIT, not the 3x to 5x claimed, which puts one 1440p frame of standard50 at 372 ms on a desktop interpreter before д13's perturbation set (922 ms with it, a defense the design does not know exists because FAILURE-MODES.md postdates it), before a phone core, before full100's 540 bubbles, and before rule 3 asks for three frames. The design earns credit for naming the layoutSheet QR-generation tax and the module-scope TextDecoder crash as upstream PRs rather than working around them silently; it loses it again by putting the QR decode on the platform barcode API, which makes the self-describing path the only path CI cannot measure, in a design whose entire justification is that CI measures the code that ships. Salvage the no-warp millimetre sampler, the banned-transcendentals test, the refusal-with-a-named-cause discipline and the timing-mark geometry verification. Do not carry over the forward model as the calibration authority, and do not carry over the rule that only constants may move: that rule is what would let this ship.

verdicts.designName: Millimetre-native scanner: no warp, no OpenCV, no photograph needed to prove it
verdicts.lens: Coverage of docs/FAILURE-MODES.md: the scanner-resident defenses د7 to د16 and د20, and acceptance criteria 10 to 19
verdicts.strongest: The measurement primitive itself: a deterministic hexagonal lattice defined in MILLIMETRES, projected forward through H into the original full resolution pixels, with two point photometric calibration taken from targets the sheet already prints (median of the four fiducial interiors plus that row's own timing mark for black, each bubble's own annulus for white). This is د7 written before د7 existed, and it pays three times over. It makes د11 free rather than a fix, because nothing is ever downscaled or resampled for measurement, so the 0.64 px per module class of defect cannot recur anywhere in the measurement path. It makes criterion 13's plus or minus 10 percent exposure term a no op by construction, since both references move with the illumination. And because the page is never warped, running criterion 13's deterministic perturbation set on a REAL golden photograph is a cheap perturbation of H followed by a re sample of the same pixels, not a re warp, which is the only architecture in front of you that can run criterion 13 over the whole corpus instead of over three shots. Graft the lattice, the mm keying, the annulus-as-local-white, and the per row black from the timing mark, verbatim.
verdicts.fatalFlaw: د10 is not merely absent, it is inverted. The design has no saturation channel anywhere, and its photometry actively destroys the evidence: d_i = clamp((W_i - m_i)/(W_i - K_row), 0, 1). A specular highlight on graphite makes the disc BRIGHTER than the surrounding paper, so the numerator goes negative and the clamp maps the single most documented failure mode in the whole research corpus (source 1, 2 and 3 all name glare as the first cause of misreads) onto exactly 0.00 ink. Then the design's own absolute floor finishes the job: max f < F_BLANK 0.30 makes the group `blank`, which in this design is a CONFIDENT, unflagged, terminal state that appears in ScanCounts.blank next to the student's genuine blanks. There is no glare tag, no unmeasurable state, no frame rejection, no quadrant instruction, and `low_contrast` cannot fire because W minus K is locally healthy (about 165 of 255) precisely when glare is worst. The design mentions glare once, in its risk list, and mitigates it with the sentence "a global glare or ink shift cancels", which is a category error: glare is a local specular spot, not a global shift, and the local calibration the design is proud of is what converts it into a zero. Downstream this poisons three more items. Criterion 10 ("one wrong answer on a glare sheet fails the build") cannot be satisfied and, worse, cannot even be MEASURED by this design's test gates, because its top gate counts bubbles "whose decided state differs from truth while not flagged uncertain" and a wrongly blank group is decided, not uncertain, so the gate reports green. Criterion 12 requires the determinism digest to compare glare and escape tags, which do not exist here. And د13's warning is realised exactly: a phone on a desk stand holds the highlight still, so three consecutive frames agree on the same wrong reading, `agree()` returns ok, and `trackSheet`'s ROI locking makes the frames MORE correlated, not less. Two supporting gaps in the same family, both structural rather than cosmetic. (1) د9's escape ring is present as geometry but repurposed as a white reference and can never be promoted to its real job: the design chose 1.15r to 1.55r (2.30 to 3.10 mm) to get better white statistics, and on full100's 5.4 mm id grid the neighbouring bubble's printed ring starts at 3.24 mm, leaving 0.14 mm of clearance, which is less than half a pixel at the design's own accepted MIN_PX_PER_MM of 3.0 (one pixel is 0.333 mm). د9 chose 1.1r to 1.4r (2.80 mm, 0.44 mm clear) precisely so the ring contains no printed ink BY CONSTRUCTION. The design also never mentions د9's stated mask for placement: 'external', where the label slot spans 2.00 to 5.20 mm from the bubble centre and therefore overlaps the annulus. So the ink-left-the-bubble signature, which is the named defense against the cross out and the circled letter that becomes the max(fill) denominator, is not merely missing, it is foreclosed at these radii. (2) د14's second half is absent from the output type. standard50 prints a keyVersion bubbleGrid (verified: gridFields = studentId 4 columns, keyVersion 1 column, 55 groups), and FAILURE-MODES places the multi key stop in the scanner and calls it HARSHER than the id rule because its failure is silent at about 25 percent on four choices. The design's read/sheet.ts assembles only the student id, and ScanCounts is {doubleMarked, blank, uncertainBubbles, idStatus}. keyVersion appears nowhere in the design. Finally, criterion 14 is entirely unbuilt: the design has at least six independent refusal paths (bad_frame, no_sheet with three stages, frame_ambiguous, low_contrast per corner, too_far, spec_mismatch from the 70 percent timing gate) plus a deliberate no-recovery policy on a damaged corner, and its test plan gates only on accuracy and zero silent errors, with no rejection ceiling, no warning ceiling, no ordinary versus adversarial strata, and no per stratum floor. Its own stated priority, "accuracy can be traded, silence cannot", is verbatim the one way ratchet criterion 14 was written to forbid.
verdicts.concreteFailure: standard50 on A4, phone flash on, sheet at 6 px/mm. Question 12 answered B in 2B pencil; the highlight covers about 35 percent of the inner 0.70r disc. Sampled values: annulus 70th percentile W = 205, row timing mark K_row = 38, disc mean over the ~120 lattice points m = 214 (saturated 250 over the highlight, graphite 190 elsewhere). Then d_B = clamp((205 - 214)/(205 - 38), 0, 1) = 0.000, and after baseline b_B about 0.02, f_B = 0.000. The three unmarked bubbles read m about 202, d about 0.018, f about 0.000. max f = 0.00, which is below F_BLANK = 0.30, so question 12 is emitted as `blank`, incremented into ScanCounts.blank, and NOT into uncertainBubbles. The frame passes every gate: pxPerMm 6.0 is above the 3.0 floor, W - K = 167 is far above the MIN_CONTRAST of 40, all 25 timing marks are found, and the geometry verification score is about 0.7. With the phone resting on a stand the highlight is fixed, so readingDigest is byte identical across frames 1, 2 and 3 and agree() returns ok. The teacher sees "1 blank" on a paper that also has genuine blanks and accepts it. The student loses a mark that is physically present on the paper, and the build's silent error counter reports zero because the state was decided, not flagged. Second, cheaper number from the same design: MIN_PX_PER_MM = 3.0 puts the printed code at 0.5 * 3.0 = 1.50 px per module, exactly half the 3 px per module floor د11 states and derives the "move closer" refusal from, so the design's own resolution gate admits frames on which the self describing path is undecodable, and it never computes px per module at all because it delegated the decode to a platform barcode API that does not exist in Node.
verdicts.salvage: Four changes, and the architecture makes all four cheap because it already owns every pixel it reads. (1) Split the disc statistic in the sample loop, which already visits every lattice point: alongside the mean, count points above 0.95 of the locally expected white from د7. Above about 10 percent of disc area the bubble is UNMEASURABLE, a fifth per bubble state that may go to uncertain but may never go to empty or blank, and remove the lower clamp on d so a negative numerator is diagnosed rather than erased. Aggregate saturated area per page quadrant and reject the FRAME, not the question, with a new closed enum member carrying the quadrant and a movement instruction. (2) Move the annulus in to 1.1r to 1.4r as د9 specifies (0.44 mm of clearance on full100 instead of 0.14 mm), mask it on the label side when placement is 'external', and compute two statistics from the same samples: the 70th percentile as the white reference, and the dark fraction as the escape signal with its own tag. This is the only change that must happen before the constants are frozen, because the radii are load bearing in two directions at once. (3) Widen the reading type: a per bubble decision margin as д13 demands rather than bands alone, an escape tag, a glare tag, a five symbol marks string that includes eraser trace, an engineVersion, and a four state keyVersion reading beside studentId, with the digest covering all of them so criteria 12, 19 and د20 become reachable. (4) Rewrite the test gates around criterion 14 before the corpus exists: stratify the seeded sweep into ordinary and adversarial layers, assert rejection at or under 2 percent and warnings at or under 2 percent on the ordinary layer, print accuracy and rejection together in the CI report, and fail on any single stratum under 98 percent. Also make agreement mean what د13 says it means: refuse to count two frames as agreeing unless the corners moved at least 2 percent of page width, and when the pose is static past 1.5 seconds run the deterministic perturbation set at RUNTIME (which costs one perturbed H and a re sample here, unlike a warp based design) instead of counting three identical frames. Two smaller ones: add a timing residual gate at 0.5 mm RMS and an exact mark count rather than the 70 percent tolerance, since د12 names the one row shift as the worst thing this product can produce, and 30 percent of marks may currently be missing and silently interpolated; and either pull the code decode inside core-omr so its px per module floor is enforceable and testable in CI, or state plainly that the self describing path is untested, which contradicts the design's own thesis.
verdicts.verdict: Defense by defense. د7 photometric calibration from the sheet: carries NATURALLY, and better than the doc asks, since it uses the fiducial interiors, the per row timing mark and a per bubble local white, which is exactly the two point per row scheme د7 describes, arrived at independently. د8 absolute floor and blank as a third state: carries NATURALLY. Proven defect (a) is fixed BY CONSTRUCTION, not mentioned: blank is a first class group state below F_BLANK 0.30, the counts include it, and 4 percent dust yields f about 0.04 which is nowhere near the floor. Two caveats. The floor is only safe BECAUSE of د7, which the design understands, but its value (0.30, with F_DEAD 0.20 and F_SURE 0.35) will be calibrated against the team's own rasteriser, and the design's tier 3 anti circularity check validates GEOMETRY against the Typst SVG, never PHOTOMETRY, so the one number that repairs the proven defect is the one number their circularity defense cannot reach. And the [0.20, 0.30) whole group uncertain band quietly reintroduces the other half of the د8 complaint: a truly untouched row with a speck near that band interrupts the teacher, which criterion 11 forbids by demanding '?' in 100 percent of clean cases. د9 inner disc and escape ring: HALF. Inner disc at 0.70r is sound and more conservative than د9's 0.75r. The escape ring is geometrically present but semantically repurposed as a white reference, has no tag, has no external placement mask, and at 1.55r sits 0.14 mm from full100's neighbouring printed ring, so it structurally cannot be promoted later without changing the radii. د10 glare: STRUCTURALLY ABSENT AND INVERTED, see the fatal flaw. د11 measure off the full resolution frame: carries NATURALLY for everything the engine measures, and this is the cleanest resolution of the ×0.25 contradiction of the four constraints; proven defect (b) is genuinely fixed for fill ratios, timing marks and fiducial refinement. It is DISPLACED, not fixed, for the code itself: the decode is handed to a platform barcode API, which means the self describing path (the product's headline promise) has zero CI coverage in a design whose entire thesis is that CI must certify what ships, and MIN_PX_PER_MM 3.0 equals 1.5 px per module against د11's floor of 3. د12 timing marks: carries NATURALLY for row registration, and its stage 10 use of timing mark energy as geometry verification is a genuinely original answer to a hard problem, because د16's corner aspect check is IMPOSSIBLE from four points alone (any quadrilateral maps exactly onto any assumed mm rectangle, leaving no residual) and this design is the one that noticed. But it drops د12's other two uses: no geometry residual gate at 0.5 mm RMS, no exact mark count (70 percent found is accepted and the rest interpolated, where the doc demands "we expected 40 and found 39" as a named refusal), no defense against injected spurious marks in the 4 mm by 5 mm window, and no x direction evidence at all, since the marks are left edge only, so a curled sheet has its column 2 and 3 x error unmeasured and unrefused. د13 decision margin and perturbation set: HALF, and the wrong half. The perturbation set exists only in CI, never at runtime, and `agree()` compares digests with no pose difference requirement, which is precisely the "repetition is not evidence" failure the doc names; the per bubble decision margin is implied by band widths rather than emitted. On the other side, this design measures cross pose sigma and gates the half band at 4 sigma, which is the most serious engagement with margin any of these designs shows. د14 grids never resolved and partial as a fourth state: first half carries NATURALLY (four states, column mask, id as a string preserving leading zeros, unset never zero); second half, the multi key stop, is ABSENT from the output type although standard50 prints a keyVersion grid. د15 closed rejection enum: carries NATURALLY in SHAPE (typed union, never a free string, `never` exhaustiveness) but roughly half in MEMBERSHIP, missing glare, bitonal, wrong exam, wrong print scale, timing residual and margin under floor, so criterion 16's requirement that the emitted cause match the injected defect above 90 percent per stratum cannot pass on those strata. د16: geometry gate substituted defensibly; the bitonal and JBIG2/MRC gates sit structurally outside the GrayImage boundary this design chose and are never named as an upstream requirement, though the design partly escapes the bitonal concern by accident, since an area integral over 120 lattice points still yields a graded coverage number where a per bubble threshold would not; write before card is correctly out of scope. د20 marks string: 4 of the 5 alphabet symbols exist, eraser trace does not, and with no glare or escape tags and no engineVersion on the reading, criterion 19's field by field reproduction of the record cannot be satisfied. Criteria: 10 FAILS structurally; 11 mostly passes with the [0.20, 0.30) caveat; 12 FAILS on the missing tags; 13 passes and is the best served of any part of this design; 14 FAILS entirely and is the criterion this particular design most needed, since it refuses on six independent axes and instruments none of them; 15 passes on uniform scale (H absorbs it, so byte identical grades across 90 to 104 percent is nearly free here) and is weak on injected or hidden marks; 16 partial; 17 fine at runtime; 18 and 19 are storage layer, with 19 blocked by the marks string. Net: this design covers more of a document it never saw than it has any right to, because it independently rediscovered د7, د8 and د11, and its no warp millimetre lattice is the best measurement primitive on the table. But it fails the single failure mode the research names first, it fails it in the confident direction, its own success metric cannot see that failure, and its rejection surface is large and unmeasured. Build the sampler and the photometry from this one; do not build its decision layer, its output type or its test gates without the four repairs above.

synthesis:
# CORE-OMR: architecture decisions

> Successor to the four independent proposals in `docs/research/raw/`. Reconciled against `docs/FAILURE-MODES.md`, which did not exist when those were written.
> Status: proposed for implementation. Date: 2026-08-15.
> Written in English here for the judgement round. The version that lands in `docs/` is Arabic, per `STATUS.md` section 10. Code comments stay English either way.

Everything below marked **[measured]** was produced by running code in this repository during this session. **[computed]** means arithmetic on constants that are in the repository. **[reasoned]** means an argument with no measurement behind it yet. Mixing the three is worse than fewer claims.

---

## Part A: the decisions

### 1. The OpenCV contradiction: no CV library on either target

**Decision.** `core-omr` is pure TypeScript over one input type, an 8 bit luminance plane. There is no OpenCV, no WASM, no native module, and no pluggable CV port with two implementations. It runs identically under Hermes and under Node from one source. `PLAN.md` section 4's four OpenCV verbs are read as a statement of intent and each is replaced by a structure exploiting equivalent:

| Plan verb | Replacement | Why the general tool is not needed |
|---|---|---|
| `resize x0.25` | Stride decimation to a fixed pixel budget, used **only to find the sheet** (defense د11) | Decimation is for locating four 8 mm squares, never for measuring |
| `adaptiveThreshold (Gaussian, 25)` | Int32 summed area table, Bradley mean threshold, on the decimated frame only | A solid 8 mm square is not a 1 px text stroke; the Gaussian buys nothing, and mean over an integral is integer and therefore bit identical across engines |
| `findContours` + area/ratio filter | Run length encoding plus union find labelling, with per label area, bbox and integer moments | We want blob statistics, not boundary chains. Suzuki-Abe would be 400 lines whose output ordering is itself a determinism hazard |
| `getPerspectiveTransform` | Hartley normalised DLT, 8x8 Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting, ties to lower row index | Four correspondences exactly, no solver library, only `+ - * /` |
| `warpPerspective to 1000x1414` | **Deleted.** See decision 2 | It is aspect wrong for four of six papers and it inserts a resampling stage between the sensor and the decision |

**Rationale, in order of weight.**

(a) `PLAN.md` section 1 calls testing these packages in CI with no phone "the architectural secret that gives us confidence in the accuracy". If the phone ran OpenCV and CI ran a TypeScript stand in, the 99.7 percent gate would measure code that never ships, and a `fast-opencv` version bump could move the number with no TypeScript diff. One implementation, one set of numbers.

(b) The sheet is not a general document. Four solid squares at known millimetres, a timing mark per question row, and a code carrying the whole geometry mean we are not detecting a page, we are verifying a known page. Detection has one job: find four blobs.

(c) Cost. **[measured]** `full100` on A4 carries 540 bubbles in 104 groups. At roughly 130 disc samples plus 96 ring samples per bubble that is about 122,000 samples per sheet, against 1.41 M bilinear fetches for the warp alone. Deleting the warp is the single largest compute saving available.

**Alternative rejected: `react-native-fast-opencv` on device with a Node or WASM equivalent in CI.** This is the obvious compromise and it is the wrong one. The seam must carry `Mat` objects, which cannot exist in Node, so the two backends differ in more than speed; and it drags `frame.dispose()`, `mat.release()` and `AsyncRunner` (PLAN rules 4 and 5) into a package the plan requires to know nothing about the camera.

**Alternative rejected: a native fast path with a "bit identical output" contract.** The only way a native kernel recovers an order of magnitude is NEON reductions and FMA contraction, and both change summation order and rounding on the binary64 accumulations that sit upstream of our single threshold. Compile with `-ffp-contract=off` and unvectorised reductions to keep bit identity and you give back most of the speed; ship it anyway and CI measures one program while the teacher runs another.

**What this decision costs, stated plainly.**

1. No general purpose fallback. A torn corner is a scan we refuse, not a scan we recover. That is deliberate: a teacher re-aims in one second and a wrong grade is unrecoverable.
2. We write and own roughly 800 lines of QR decoding and 700 lines of image primitives, with no upstream bugfix stream. **[measured]** The working tree already contains a prototype of this shape: `src/qr/` is 8 files totalling 891 lines, no file over 145, and `vitest run` passes 36 tests in `packages/core-omr`. The cost is proven payable.
3. We give up `cornerSubPix`, RANSAC and decades of hardening on general documents.
4. **We accept a Hermes performance ceiling we must measure, and we forbid ourselves the escape hatch.** If Hermes is too slow the answer is to do less work, not to add a backend. Decision 18 says how.

---

### 2. The frame is never warped: measurement is forward sampling in paper millimetres

**Decision.** The homography `H` maps sheet millimetres to source pixels and is used forward only. Every measured quantity (bubble disc, escape ring, timing mark, code module, name crop) is a fixed set of positions **defined in page millimetres**, pushed through `H`, and read on the original frame with bilinear interpolation. Nothing is resampled into a canonical page.

**Rationale.** Two photographs of one paper are two different pixel arrays. If the estimator is an integral over a resampled 1000 px grid, the grid lands on different graphite each shot, so the estimator itself moves with pose. A lattice fixed in millimetres integrates the **same physical points on the paper** in both shots, and the only pose dependence left is homography residual, which we measure and gate at 0.5 mm RMS (د12). This is not a purity argument, it is the reproducibility mechanism, and it is also cheaper.

Two contradictions dissolve for free. `1414/1000 = 1.414` fits A4 (1.4143), A5 (1.4189) and A6 (1.4095) and distorts LETTER (1.2917), HALF_LETTER (1.5540) and QUARTER_LETTER (1.2870); with no warp target there is nothing to distort. And measuring on the full resolution frame is the only thing the code can express, which is defense د11 carried by construction rather than by discipline.

**Alternative rejected: warp once, sample cheaply afterwards.** It looks cheaper per bubble and is not: 1.41 M destination pixels against 122,000 samples, plus an interpolation kernel whose phase is a function of pose sitting directly upstream of the number determinism depends on.

---

### 3. The input contract carries its photometric provenance

**Decision.**

```ts
export interface PixelSource {
  readonly kind: 'cameraPlane' | 'decodedStill' | 'scanner' | 'synthetic';
  /** Transfer curve the values are encoded with. Linearised at ingest. */
  readonly transfer: 'linear' | 'srgb' | 'bt709';
  readonly range: 'full' | 'video';
  readonly luma: 'bt601' | 'bt709' | 'measured';
}

export interface GrayImage {
  readonly data: Uint8Array;
  readonly width: number;
  readonly height: number;
  /** Bytes per row. Android Y planes pad rows; ignoring this shears the image. */
  readonly rowStride: number;
  /** Bytes per pixel within a row. YUV_420_888 permits values above 1. */
  readonly pixelStride: number;
  readonly source: PixelSource;
}
```

Ingest applies a 256 entry linearisation LUT (built once) and a video range expansion, so every stage downstream sees linear reflectance proportional values.

**Rationale.** Our two targets do not deliver the same pixels. CI decodes stills or renders synthetics in linear coverage; the phone delivers gamma encoded, sometimes video range luma. Two point calibration pins the endpoints but not the curvature between them. **[computed]** With paper at 248, a mid grey pencil at 150 and toner at 18, linear ink is `(248-150)/(248-18) = 0.426`; after a 1/2.2 encode the same physical mark measures `(251.8-200.5)/(251.8-73.8) = 0.288`. A 0.14 shift in ink across the same threshold band is not a tuning difference, it is a different answer. The whole case for one source is that the accuracy number transfers, and it does not transfer unless the pixels mean the same thing.

Two consequences we accept. The floor survives the curvature (the printed glyph baseline compresses down with it, from 0.07 to 0.043 **[computed]**, so the floor stays 5.8x above it), but the **light mark** end does not: a genuine mark at true ink 0.30 can measure 0.20 and read as empty. That is a false blank, a criterion 11 failure. So the golden set is stratified by `PixelSource.kind` and criterion 14's per stratum 98 percent floor applies to the strata, which is exactly what criterion 14 was written for.

**Alternative rejected: "the Y plane is already grayscale, so conversion costs nothing".** True about the sample rate and false about the values, and the failure is silent and CI green.

### 4. Photometry: two fields, not two numbers (defense د7)

**Decision.** The sheet prints its own photometric reference and nobody was reading it. We recover two fields over the page:

- **`W(x, y)`, the illumination field**, in code values. Fast varying, many samples.
- **`k(x, y)`, the toner reflectance**, dimensionless, `K/W`. Slow varying, few anchors.
- Then `K(x, y) = k(x, y) * W(x, y)`, and ink is measured on the `K` to `W` scale.

**Anchors.**

| Field | Source | Count on `standard50` **[measured]** |
|---|---|---|
| `k` | Interior of each of the 4 fiducial squares (a 5x5 mm patch inset 1.5 mm) | 4 |
| `k`, per row | Interior of that row's timing mark (inset 0.8 mm) | 25 |
| `W` | Escape ring 70th percentile of every bubble (decision 6) | 294 |
| `W` | White rails: the inter column gaps (`columnGapMm` 6) and the sidebar gap (`sidebarGapMm` 8) at each row's centre line | about 25 |

**Fitting.** `W` is a bilinear `w0 + w1*x + w2*y + w3*x*y` by normal equations on a 4x4, closed form, with exactly one robustness pass (drop residuals over 2.5 sigma, refit once, never a convergence loop). `k` is bilinear over the four fiducials, then **corrected per row** by the residual measured at that row's own timing mark, with rows whose mark was not found inheriting by linear interpolation between the nearest found marks.

**Rationale, and why the split matters.** A hard shadow crossing one row is the named failure د7 exists for, and a single bilinear black surface cannot represent it. But illumination is multiplicative and toner reflectance is a property of the toner, not of the light. Putting the fast variation in `W` (hundreds of samples, one per bubble) and the slow variation in `k` (29 anchors, per row corrected) puts each estimator where its data is. A shadow then moves `W` at the bubble and leaves `k` alone, and `ink = (W_local - core) / (W_local * (1 - k))` is correct through it.

`W_local(b)` is the bubble's own escape ring 70th percentile when the ring dark fraction is under 0.25, and the fitted `W(x, y)` otherwise. The 0.25 switch is what stops a strike through from silently depressing the white reference for its whole row.

**Guard.** If `W * (1 - k) < 40` grey levels anywhere a bubble sits, the frame is refused as `low_contrast`. Never a graded sheet on a frame that cannot separate ink from paper.

**Alternative rejected: one white and one black per group** (the group's own 85th percentile, or a global fiducial level rescaled). It makes the white reference a function of how many bubbles the student shaded. **[computed]** On a True/False question where both bubbles are shaded, a group percentile white lands on graphite, the ink ratio collapses, and a double shaded question is reported as blank.

**Alternative rejected: normalising against a page wide quantile pair** (`(f - q30) / (q95 - q30)`). This is `fill_i / max(fill)` with a larger window and a 5 percent trim, and it re-commits the proven defect at page scope. **[measured]** `full100` has 540 bubbles, so `q95` is the 27th darkest; a student who answers 22 of 100 questions has 26 filled bubbles, so the peak is computed from an empty bubble and the spread collapses. The cliff is at 10 of 50 on `standard50` and 2 of 20 on `quick20`.

### 5. The ink scale, the absolute floor, and blank as a third state (defense د8)

**Decision.** `ink` is in `[0, 1]`, where 0 is this paper under this light at this point and 1 is this sheet's own printed toner. **No ratio is computed until the darkest bubble in a group clears an absolute floor measured on that scale.** Below the floor the group is **blank**, which is a decided state and a different word from ambiguous in the interface: the first is the student's decision, the second is our failure.

The numbers, with provenance, are in Part D. The floor is `MIN_INK = 0.25`.

Two further clauses from د8, both load bearing:

1. **If every bubble in a group clears the floor, the group is ambiguous, not biggest wins.** This is the dirty platen and sheen case.
2. **The measurement is on the corrected grey image, never on the binary mask** built to find the corners, because binarising destroys exactly the gradient the fill ratio exists to preserve.

**Alternative rejected: subtracting a measured per symbol baseline before the floor.** The printed letter inside a bubble is real (default `placement` is `internal`) and subtracting it is tempting. But estimating it as a low percentile of that symbol's own population has a hard cliff: once more than 75 percent of the bubbles carrying one symbol are shaded, the 25th percentile lands inside the filled cluster, the baseline jumps, and every mark of that symbol clamps to zero. That is reachable on a True/False sheet, on a `select: 'many'` set, and on a zero heavy student id. Instead we make the floor immune by arithmetic: **[computed]** from `theme.ts` and `grid.ts`, a 1.9 mm glyph covers 7 to 11 percent of the 1.5 mm radius disc, and the label reflectances are 0.690 (light), 0.549 (normal) and 0.416 (dark), so an empty internal bubble sits at ink 0.02 to 0.07. `MIN_INK = 0.25` is 3.5x the worst case. The measured baseline is still computed, but as a **diagnostic that gates rather than a number that moves a threshold**: if the median ink of sub floor bubbles exceeds `0.5 * MIN_INK`, the frame's photometry is not what we calibrated and it is refused.

### 6. Inner disc and escape ring, clamped per sheet (defense د9)

**Decision.** Two concentric sample sets per bubble, both defined in units of the bubble radius `r`:

- **Inner disc, radius `0.75 r`.** At `r = 2` that is 1.5 mm. **[computed]** The printed outline's inner edge sits at `r - stroke/2 = 1.84 mm` at the darkest theme (`bubbleStrokeMm` 0.32), so the clearance is 0.34 mm. The outline is excluded from the numerator entirely, which is why the three darkness levels cannot move the measurement.
- **Escape ring, `1.20 r` to `1.40 r`,** clamped per sheet:

```
escapeInner = max(1.20 * r,  r + MAX_STROKE_MM / 2 + 0.20)
escapeOuter = min(1.40 * r,  minPitchMm - r - MAX_STROKE_MM / 2 - 0.35)
```

`MAX_STROKE_MM = 0.32`, the darkest theme. **[measured]** On `full100`, `minPitch` is `gridPitchYMm = 5.4` (min centre to centre 5.400 mm across all 540 bubbles), giving `escapeInner = 2.4`, `escapeOuter = 2.8`, with 0.24 mm of clearance from our own outline and 0.44 mm from the nearest neighbour's ink. On `quick20` and `standard50`, `minPitch = 5.6` and the ring is the same. If `escapeOuter - escapeInner < 0.30 mm` the ring is unusable for that spec, the escape channel is **disabled and reported as disabled** on the reading, and `W_local` comes from the fitted field alone.

**The ring carries two independent statistics, and this is the correction to every proposal that used it for one purpose only:**

| Statistic | Use |
|---|---|
| 70th percentile of ring samples | `W_local`, the per bubble paper white (د7) |
| Fraction of ring samples above an ink threshold of 0.18 | The **escape tag** (د9): ink that left the bubble |

**Masking.** When `spec.questions[n-1].placement === 'external'`, the ring sector within 40 degrees of the negative x axis is dropped. **[computed]** `grid.ts` puts the label anchor 3.6 mm left of the bubble centre at `choiceLabelMm` 2.3, so its ink reaches to 2.4 mm left of centre, inside a 2.8 mm ring.

**Alternative rejected: a wider ring at 1.15 r to 1.55 r** for better white statistics. **[computed]** At `full100`'s 5.4 mm grid pitch the neighbour's ink starts at 3.24 mm and a 3.1 mm outer radius leaves 0.14 mm, under any plausible registration budget. Better white statistics bought by sampling the neighbour's ink is not better white.

### 7. Glare is its own channel and rejects the frame, not the question (defense د10)

**Decision.** Glare is not light on top of a reading, it is the reading destroyed. The disc sampler returns three numbers, not one:

```ts
interface DiscStat {
  readonly mean: number;          // code values
  readonly saturated: number;     // count of samples at or above 0.95 * W_local
  readonly total: number;
}
```

Rules, exactly as د10 states them:

1. `saturated / total > 0.10` makes the bubble **unmeasurable**. It routes to uncertain and **never to empty**.
2. A core mean **above** `W_local` (a negative ink before any clamp) is by definition specular. It is tagged, never silently clamped to zero.
3. The **frame** is rejected, not the question, with the quadrant of the page holding the most saturation and a direction to move. PLAN rule 5 drops frames for free already, and the next frame from another angle is clean.

**Rationale.** This is the first named cause of misreads at three independent vendors and criterion 10 drops the build on one silent wrong answer under it. A mean is the one operator that cannot represent missing information: **[computed]** with `W = 205`, `K = 38`, graphite at 25 and a highlight covering 35 percent of the disc, the mean is 25*0.65 + 255*0.35 = 105.5, so ink = `(205-105.5)/(205-38) = 0.596`, still a mark; at 60 percent coverage the mean is 163 and ink is 0.251, right at the floor; at 65 percent it is under the floor and the shaded bubble reports **blank**. Every determinism mechanism then confirms the error: a phone on a desk holds the highlight still, three frames agree, and the perturbation set re-samples the same saturated pixels. The saturation count is the only thing that sees it, and the 130 disc samples that hold the answer are already in memory.

**Ordering note.** `W_local` comes from the ring, so the sampler computes ring statistics first and disc statistics second, over sample arrays it already holds. There is no second pass and no architectural cost.

### 8. Full resolution measurement and a px per module floor (defense د11)

**Decision.** Decimation is used **to find the sheet and for nothing else**. The homography is solved on the decimated frame, corners are refined at full resolution (decision 9), and then every measurement (fill ratios, timing marks, code modules, name crop) is taken from the frame at its native resolution.

Two measured gates, both named refusals:

- **Page:** local `pxPerMm` under `MIN_PX_PER_MM = 6.0` refuses with `resolution_low { need: 'page' }`. د11 derives this: 3 px per 0.5 mm code module means the page must span at least 1260 px.
- **Code:** px per module on the actual code crop under `MIN_MODULE_PX = 3.0` refuses with `resolution_low { need: 'code' }` and the message "come closer", **before** any decode is attempted.

**[computed]** At 1080p over 210 mm the module is 2.57 px (marginal, matching 4ب-7); at 1440p it is 3.43 px (works); at 2160p it is 5.14 px. This is why 4ب-7 mandates a 1440p or better frame format and accepts the frame rate cost.

**Alternative rejected: `MIN_PX_PER_MM = 3.0`,** which several proposals chose because a 4 mm bubble is still 12 px across at that density. It admits frames on which the self describing path, the product's headline promise, cannot work, and it admits them silently.

### 9. The timing marks are read, and one reading serves three purposes (defense د12)

**Decision.** `PLAN.md` section 3 promises the marks fix the row index and section 4's pipeline never touches them. They are read, and the one reading does three jobs:

1. **Row registration.** Each row's y is set from its own mark, not from interpolation alone, giving a piecewise linear per row correction applied to every bubble in that row in every column.
2. **Geometry proof.** The RMS residual between predicted and measured mark centres detects, with one mechanism, paper curl, feeder stretch, copy generation scale drift and a fold. **[computed]** د12's budget: at 6 px/mm one pixel is 0.167 mm, so a gate at `MAX_RESIDUAL_MM = 0.5` RMS is 3 px and easily measurable, while a mark 4 mm tall is centroided to about 0.2 mm. These are the cases where the four corners solve perfectly and the error lives in the middle of the page.
3. **Counting.** The expected count is known from the spec. **[measured]** `quick20` 20 marks, `standard50` 25, `full100` 34. "Expected 34, found 33" is the named refusal `timing_marks_missing`, never a silent renumbering of every row below it.

**Matching is by nearest neighbour to the predicted position, never by order.** A one row shift does not damage a grade, it invents a whole paper with total confidence, and universities specify rejecting a sheet for exactly this reason.

**Search window and detection.** The window is 11 mm wide by 8 mm tall around the predicted centre, at full resolution. Inside it we run the same connected components pass used for the fiducials and take the component whose bounding box best matches the expected 6 x 4 mm, rejecting the others. **A window sized to the mark itself is not a measurement:** a 30 x 30 px window at 11.5 px/mm is 2.6 mm square, fits entirely inside the mark, has no bimodality, and returns a residual of identically 0.00 mm on every row of every paper, which passes the gate and disables it. Component matching also handles criterion 15's injected spurious marks and a pen line drawn over a mark.

The same window supplies the mark's interior black level for the per row `k` correction in decision 4. Locating a mark and then discarding its grey value is throwing away the one number that makes a shadow across one row a measurement instead of a guess.

### 10. Decision margin, and what replaces "three consecutive frames" (defense د13)

**Decision.** Every bubble and every group carries a **decision margin in ink units**: the distance from the quantity that decided it to the nearest threshold it would have had to cross. A group whose margin is under `MARGIN_FLOOR` is promoted to uncertain regardless of what the rule concluded.

PLAN rule 3 as written is repetition, not evidence: a still phone under a still lamp gives three identical frames, and a specular highlight is constant across all three. So:

- **Frame agreement counts only between measurably different poses.** `agree()` takes the pose with each reading and requires corner movement of at least 2 percent of page width or 3 degrees of view angle before two frames count as agreeing.
- **When the phone is still for more than 1.5 seconds** (the tripod and the flatbed scanner, and the PDF path where consecutive frames do not exist at all), the frame set is replaced by the **deterministic perturbation set**: the same pixels re-measured under fixed perturbations of `H`, requiring an identical complete result.

The perturbation set is a fixed enumeration, never random:

| Set | Members | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Runtime (replaces rule 3 when still) | 4: `(±1.5 deg) x (±2 percent scale)`, each with a 1 px translation in a rotating quadrant | about 4 x 122,000 = 490,000 sample reads, against د13's 226,000 budget note, and it is measurement only with no re-detection |
| CI (criterion 13) | 81: the 3x3x3 grid of `{-1, 0, +1}` on rotation, scale and translation, crossed with exposure at `{-10, 0, +10} percent` | Build gate, run over every golden paper |

Exposure perturbation is a multiplicative gain applied to sampled code values before photometry. Because the photometry is a ratio of differences it should cancel exactly, and the test that it does is the point.

**The closure that makes this worth building:** criterion 13 says an answer that flips under the perturbation set "is a bubble whose decision margin was underestimated, and that is a defect in the margin calculation, not in the threshold". So criterion 13 is the **test of the margin model**, not of the thresholds, and a flip is a bug with a known location.

### 11. The bridge over `BubbleGroup`, and never matching on a field id

**Decision.** `bubbleGroups()` returns `{ id, bubbles }` and nothing else. `plan/groups.ts` rebuilds what the scanner needs, and it does so **positionally**:

- **`select`**: walk `layout.questionColumns[*].rows[*]`, take `row.question`, and read `spec.questions[row.question - 1].select`. There is no exported group id parser and we do not write one.
- **`placement`**: the same lookup, needed because د9 masks the ring on the label side when placement is `external`.
- **`usage`**: pair `layout.gridFields[i]` with the `i`-th entry of `spec.headerFields.filter(kind === 'bubbleGrid')`. **Never** match on the string `'studentId'`.

**Rationale, verified by running the round trip.** `decode.ts:70` synthesises `id: f${index}` and `label: usage`, so `f:studentId:2` becomes `f:f1:2` on a device that has only ever seen the paper, while `usage` survives. Any code that finds the id grid by string works on the teacher's own device and fails on the self describing path, which is the path the product's headline promise depends on. A property test asserts that a spec and its encode-decode round trip give identical **semantic** readings from identical pixels despite differing ids.

Any index that comes back `undefined` under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` ends the scan as `spec_mismatch`. It is never defaulted.

### 12. Grids are never resolved, and the key version stops the paper (defense د14)

**Decision.** Four states, not two, for every `bubbleGrid` field:

```ts
type FieldReading =
  | { kind: 'read'; value: string }                                  // a STRING, so '0000' is an id
  | { kind: 'partial'; value: string; blankColumns: readonly number[] }
  | { kind: 'ambiguous'; columns: readonly number[] }
  | { kind: 'unset' };
```

- `unset` is never the digit zero. Zero is a valid id and inventing it merges two different states (PLAN rule 9).
- `partial` carries the column mask so the card can say "4 of 8 columns blank: 3 _ _ 7 1 _ _ 4" rather than a mangled number.
- **A grid column is always `select: 'one'`.** `BubbleGridFieldSchema` has no select mode, so two marks in a grid column are always an error and never an answer. This is stated as its own rule rather than left to a generous reading of PLAN rule 2.
- **`usage: 'keyVersion'` is stricter than the id, not laxer.** The reading carries it as its own four state field. When the exam has more than one active key and the version is `unset`, `partial` or `ambiguous`, the paper **stops and produces no grade**: no warning, no partial score, and never a positional choice of key. When the exam has one key the field is ignored entirely. Core-omr emits the state; the app owns the stop, because core-omr does not know how many keys the exam has.

**Rationale.** A wrong id produces an ownerless paper, which is audible noise. A wrong key produces about 25 percent on four choices, which is a completely plausible grade for a weak student that nobody will ever investigate.

### 13. Rejection is a closed union with a physical cause (defense د15)

**Decision.** Every refusal carries a cause from a closed union with data, never a free string. The cause is the return type, so a refusal without a cause is unrepresentable. Every `switch` over it is exhaustive with no `default`, per `CODING-STANDARDS.md` section 3 rule 5.

The full membership is in Part I. Two design rules govern it:

1. **Causes are physical, not pipeline stages.** "Stage: code" conflates too far, damaged and glare on the code. Criterion 16 audits that the emitted cause matches the injected defect above 90 percent per stratum, and a stage name cannot pass that.
2. **A confident wrong diagnosis is worse than no diagnosis**, so where two causes are genuinely indistinguishable we emit the one that is cheapest to act on and carry the measured numbers alongside.

### 14. Acceptance gates before anything is graded (defense د16)

**Decision.** Four gates, all `mvp`, and the first three run on **every** path, warm and cold alike.

1. **Histogram gate.** A two level image is refused as `bilevel_image`. Test: fewer than 12 occupied bins in a 64 bin histogram of the mid range, or over 90 percent of mass in the two extreme bins. This is the sharpest architectural collision in the whole problem: competitors accept bitonal scans because their engines decide a boolean per bubble, and Remark even prefers black and white. We cannot. In a two level image every bubble is 0 or 1, so our uncertainty mechanism reports total confidence, which is the worst possible failure for a product whose promise is that it does not guess.
2. **Geometry gate.** After the quad is refined, the measured aspect of the fiducial rectangle is compared with the paper declared in the code or the spec, with a ±2 percent tolerance. **[measured]** The six papers' `spanY/spanX` ratios are A4 1.4579, LETTER 1.3214, A5 1.4844, A6 1.5059, HALF_LETTER 1.6471, QUARTER_LETTER 1.3523. A4 against LETTER is 10.3 percent apart, so ±2 percent has an enormous margin. **A uniform print scale is not detectable from the sheet's content and is not harmful**, because every coordinate is relative to the fiducial frame and the homography absorbs it; what is harmful is non uniform distortion (A4 forced onto LETTER proportions, feeder stretch), and that is free to detect. We are the vendor who says the true thing, not the strictest thing.
3. **Multiplicity gate.** If more than four size consistent fiducial candidates survive, the frame holds more than one sheet and is refused as `multiple_sheets`. **[computed]** `sheet-pdf/src/page.ts` puts 2 or 4 A5 sheets on a landscape A4 carrier at x origins 0 and 149; the extremes of all eight fiducials form a perfectly convex rectangle of four identically sized squares spanning 277 x 190 mm, and the timing marks then land inside the real marks with a y residual of 0.00 mm, so **the timing gate does not catch it**. Only counting the candidates and checking the aspect (0.686 measured against A5's declared 1.484) does.
4. **Write before card** is the app's, listed in Part G.

**Decision.** The reading carries the evidence, not a counter. Rule 6 promises a fill ratio per bubble and a flag, and then `PLAN.md` section 5 stores `flags smallint`, so the evidence is computed, shown once and destroyed. Core-omr emits:

### 16. Determinism is engineered, and enforced by a test

**Decision.** On any path that can reach a decision, the only arithmetic is `+ - * /` and `Math.sqrt / abs / min / max / floor / round`. **Banned outright: `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `atan2`, `exp`, `log`, `pow`, `hypot`, `cbrt`, `sign`, `random`, and the `**` operator.** ECMAScript leaves the precision of the transcendentals implementation defined and Hermes and V8 disagree in the last bits.

Consequences that shape the code:

- Quad ordering uses a cross product comparator, never `atan2`.
- Distances compare squared values, or use `Math.sqrt` explicitly, never `Math.hypot`.
- The disc and ring sample lattices and the perturbation set's rotation matrices are **generated constant files** (`plan/lattice.gen.ts`, `scan/perturb.gen.ts`), because building them needs trigonometry. This is the "generated data files" exemption `CODING-STANDARDS.md` section 1 rule 3 already grants.
- Every sort carries an explicit total order comparator with an original index tiebreak, never trusting engine sort stability. Percentiles are nearest rank with no interpolation.
- No clock, no locale, no `Intl`, no randomness, no `Map`/`Set` iteration order on a decision path.
- Final ink ratios are quantised to 1/1024.

**Enforced by `test/purity.test.ts`,** which walks every file in `src/` and fails on any banned identifier. This is not hypothetical hygiene: **[measured]** the prototype in the working tree calls `Math.atan2` twice in `geometry/quad.ts:35`, and `Math.hypot` at `quad.ts:91-94`, `frame.ts:73-76`, `homography.ts:80-81`, `bubble.ts:85`, `perturb.ts:70`, and `Math.cos`/`Math.sin` at `perturb.ts:94-95`. Sixteen call sites, all replaceable, none of them noticed until a test looked.

### 18. The performance budget is measured on an interpreter, not modelled

**Decision.** Three rules, because the "no CV library" bet is only defensible if the replacement is genuinely cheaper than the library.

1. **No full frame multi scale sweep.** Fiducials are found by **one** adaptive threshold plus **one** connected components pass on a decimated frame, then filtered by fill ratio (>= 0.75), aspect (0.6 to 1.67), size bounds implied by the paper, and border contact. A seven scale box search over the whole frame is 20 M or more integral reads and is more expensive than the `findContours` it replaces.
2. **Decimation targets a pixel budget, not a short side.** `stride = ceil(sqrt(width * height / TARGET_PX))` with `TARGET_PX = 120_000`, so a 1080p frame and a 12 MP frame do the same detection work. A rule like `floor(min(w,h)/384)` inverts the cost: **[computed]** it gives a 960x540 view (518 k px) at 1080p and a 576x432 view (249 k px) at 12 MP, so the cheaper phone does twice the work of the flagship.
3. **`tools/bench.ts` runs under an actual interpreter in CI on every PR**, not under V8 with an assumed multiplier. `hermes-engine-cli` runs headless on Linux. The measured V8 to interpreter penalty on this kind of code is 11x to 26x, not the 3x to 8x every proposal assumed, and a Node gate with a fixed multiplier certifies green a pipeline that misses on the phone by an order of magnitude. The same bench catches a cost a Node gate structurally cannot see: putting a hot helper behind a module boundary, which the 300 line file cap pushes you toward, costs an interpreter roughly a third and costs V8 nothing.

**Budget arithmetic, stated so it is not quietly forgotten.** Criterion 2 allows 400 ms from sheet to result. A result requires either three agreeing frames at measurably different poses (rule 3 plus د13) or one frame plus the 4 member runtime perturbation set. So the per **frame** budget is about 130 ms and the per **measurement** budget is about 80 ms. Those two numbers are published separately and gated separately.

## Part C: the pipeline

Units are stated on every boundary. Every stage returns a value; nothing throws for an expected failure.

**Stage 1, ingest.** In: `GrayImage` plus `ScanTarget`. Out: a linearised frame handle. Validates `rowStride >= width * pixelStride`, `data.length >= rowStride * height`, both dimensions at least 640. Applies the transfer LUT and range expansion of decision 3. On the warm path the caller supplies `PreparedSheet` objects; `layoutSheet` never runs in the frame loop. *Fails:* `bad_frame { field }`.

**Stage 2, histogram gate.** In: linearised frame, subsampled every 16th pixel. Out: accept, or refuse. Runs the bilevel test of decision 14. *Fails:* `bilevel_image { occupiedBins }`.

**Stage 3, decimate and mask.** In: full frame. Out: a decimated image of about 120,000 px, its `Int32Array` integral, and a 1 bit ink mask. `stride = ceil(sqrt(w * h / 120000))`. Point sampling, not box averaging: an 8 mm fiducial photographed at 80 percent page fill survives naked subsampling and the phase of a decimation grid is fixed by the buffer, whereas a resize filter's phase is not. Mask is Bradley: ink when `pixel * count * 100 < boxSum * 88`, integer, window one eighth of the image width. *Fails:* none possible here.

**Stage 4, connected components.** In: the mask. Out: 2,000 to 6,000 labels with bbox, area and integer centroid sums. RLE per row, union find with path compression across rows, one accumulation pass. *Fails:* `noise_frame { labels }` above 40,000 labels, which means a photograph of a textured surface rather than paper.

**Stage 5, fiducial candidates and quad.** In: labels, plus the expected fiducial size range from the target's paper (or the union over all six on the cold path). Out: four refined corner estimates in decimated pixels, ordered TL, TR, BL, BR, matching `cornerFiducials`. Filter: `area / (bboxW * bboxH) >= 0.75`, aspect in `[0.6, 1.67]`, not touching the border, size within range. Order by cross product sign, never `atan2`. *Fails:* `corners_not_found { found, corners }` (the camera overlay lights the ones it has, so the teacher sees which corner is missing); `multiple_sheets { quads }` when more than four size consistent candidates survive.

**Stage 6, sub pixel refinement.** In: four coarse centres, the full resolution frame. Out: four centres to about 0.1 px. Per corner, a window 1.6x the expected fiducial side at full resolution, a 256 bin histogram, Otsu inside that window (a black square on paper is the one case Otsu is not a guess), then the centroid of the **binary** mask. Binary and not intensity weighted, because an illumination gradient across the window biases an intensity centroid and leaves a binary one unbiased. Exactly two iterations, never a tolerance loop. *Fails:* `low_contrast { corner }` when Otsu separation is under 40 grey levels on two or more corners.

**Stage 7, homography and paper.** In: four refined centres in px, four destination centres in mm **taken from `layout.fiducials`** (never hardcoded). Out: `Projector`, mm to px. Hartley normalise both point sets, build the 8x8 from rows `[X Y 1 0 0 0 -xX -xY | x]` and `[0 0 0 X Y 1 -yX -yY | y]`, Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting, denormalise. Cold path: score each of the six papers by the aspect and the fiducial size ratio and shortlist. **The geometry gate of decision 14 runs here on every path.** *Fails:* `degenerate_quad` on a near zero pivot; `geometry_mismatch { measuredAspect, declaredAspect, paper }`.

**Stage 8, resolution gate.** In: `Projector`, page size in mm. Out: `pxPerMm`. Project `(0,0)`, `(1,0)`, `(0,1)` mm and take the smaller of the two norms. *Fails:* `resolution_low { need: 'page', pxPerMm }` under 6.0.

**Stage 9, timing registration.** In: `Projector`, `layout.timingMarks` (in mm), full resolution frame. Out: a per row y correction table in mm, per row black levels in code values, and the residual RMS. Decision 9 in full. *Fails:* `timing_marks_missing { expected, found }`; `not_flat { residualMm }` above 0.5 mm RMS.

**Stage 10, printed code.** Only on the cold path or when confirming a `templateId`. In: `Projector`, full resolution frame. Out: a base32 payload, then `decodeSheetCode`. The box is at `layout.code.box`, so nothing is searched for: project its four corners, re-register locally within ±3 mm on the actual dark module bounding box (this second local homography is what absorbs the lens distortion a four corner global homography does not model), check px per module, then sample module centres as 3x3 medians. Then BCH format info, mask removal, de-interleave, Reed-Solomon, alphanumeric unpacking. **A decoded spec is never trusted: it re-enters at stage 7 as an ordinary hypothesis and must pass the geometry gate and the timing residual.** *Fails:* `resolution_low { need: 'code', pxPerModule }`; `code_unreadable { stage }`; `unknown_template`; `layout_overflow { area, axis }`.

**Stage 11, sample.** In: `Projector` with corrections, `PreparedSheet`, full resolution frame. Out: per bubble, a `DiscStat` and a `RingStat`. Disc: 131 lattice points inside `0.75 r`, each a bilinear read. Ring: 96 points over `escapeInner` to `escapeOuter` in 32 sectors, masked on the label side when `placement === 'external'`. **[measured]** 122,000 samples for `full100`'s 540 bubbles. *Fails:* `off_frame { groupId }` when over 5 percent of a bubble's lattice projects outside the frame.

**Stage 12, photometry.** In: ring statistics, fiducial interiors, per row mark blacks. Out: `W(x,y)`, `k(x,y)`, and `ink` per bubble in `[0,1]` quantised to 1/1024. Decision 4 in full. *Fails:* `low_contrast { minSeparation }` under 40 grey levels.

**Stage 13, glare.** In: disc statistics and `W_local`. Out: per bubble `unmeasurable` flags and a page saturation map. Decision 7 in full. *Fails:* `glare { quadrant, saturatedFraction }`.

**Stage 14, decide.** In: `ink` per bubble, `select` and `usage` from `plan/groups.ts`. Out: `QuestionReading` and `FieldReading` per group with margins. Part D in full. *Fails:* none. An ambiguous group is data on a successful scan, not a failed scan, because a teacher holding a 50 question paper needs the other 49.

**Stage 15, assemble.** In: everything above. Out: `SheetReading` with `answers`, `marks`, per group readings, identity, key version, `ScanCounts` (double shaded, blanks, uncertain bubbles, id status, exactly what section 4 requires on screen), `ScanQuality` (min margin, residual, saturation, `pxPerMm`, `pxPerModule`), the name crop quad in source pixels and an optional gray crop, `H`, and the pose. **Grading against the answer key stays out of this package**, because `answer_keys.extras` and `points` are editable after the fact and a key correction must never invalidate a golden set expectation. That is a deliberate deviation from section 4's last pipeline arrow, and the reason is the stability of the golden set.

**Stage 16, agreement (caller loop).** In: successive readings with poses. Out: confirmed, or continue. Decision 10.

## Part D: the confidence model, with numbers

Every bubble returns `ink: number` in `[0,1]`, never a boolean (PLAN rule 6). The scale is physical: **0 is this paper at this point under this light, 1 is this sheet's own printed toner**, recovered from the four fiducial squares and the per row timing mark, which are `#000000` at all three darkness levels **[measured]** (`theme.ts` overrides only `bubbleStroke`, `bubbleLabel`, `choiceLabel`, `frameStrokeMm`, `boxStrokeMm`).

```
ink(b) = clamp01( (W_local(b) - core(b)) / (W_local(b) * (1 - k(b))) )
```

### The constants

| Name | Value | Where it came from |
|---|---|---|
| `MIN_INK` (the floor) | **0.25** | د8 states 0.25 as the starting point. **[computed]** It is 3.5x the worst printed glyph baseline: a 1.9 mm label covers 7 to 11 percent of the 1.5 mm radius disc, and the darkest label reflectance is 0.416, so an empty internal bubble reads 0.02 to 0.07. No printed furniture can reach it. **[measured]** On synthetic sheets, dust and sensor noise land under 0.06. |
| `TRACE_INK` | **0.10** | Above the noise floor and below `MIN_INK`. A bubble here is empty for scoring and carries the `e` symbol in the marks string. **It raises no warning**, so a clean erasure does not spend criterion 14's 2 percent question warning ceiling. |
| `T_MARK` | **0.40** | **[reasoned]** A genuine light pencil after د7 calibration: disc coverage about 0.7, graphite reflectance about 0.45, giving 0.38 upward. A firm 2B is 0.72, a pen is near 0.90. An eraser ghost retains 20 to 50 percent of a full mark, so a poor erasure lands in `[0.25, 0.40)` and is surfaced while a clean one falls below the floor and is silent. **This is the most golden set dependent number in the package.** |
| Uncertain band | **`[0.25, 0.40)`** | The interval between the two above. |
| `ANSWER_RATIO` | **0.65** | PLAN rule 1, unchanged, applied after the floor. |
| `RUNNER_UP_RATIO` | **0.45** | PLAN rule 1, unchanged. |
| `MARGIN_FLOOR` | **0.06** | **[computed]** Registration sensitivity. For the worst case mark, a straight edge through the disc centre, `d(fraction)/d(delta) = 2 / (pi * R) = 2 / (pi * 1.5) = 0.424` per mm, times an ink contrast of about 0.9, gives 0.38 per mm. At a 0.15 mm registration error that is 0.057. |
| `MAX_SATURATION` | **0.10** | د10 verbatim. |
| `ESCAPE_INK` | **0.18** | **[reasoned]** Well above the ring's own noise on a clean sheet, which is near zero because the ring holds no printed ink by construction. |
| `MIN_CONTRAST` | **40 of 255** | **[reasoned]** Below this the grey band is compressed to nothing and every bubble becomes uncertain, so refusing is honest. |
| `MIN_PX_PER_MM` | **6.0** | د11: 3 px per 0.5 mm module, i.e. a page spanning 1260 px. |
| `MIN_MODULE_PX` | **3.0** | د11 verbatim. |
| `MAX_RESIDUAL_MM` | **0.5** RMS | د12 verbatim. **[computed]** 3 px at 6 px/mm, against a minimum row pitch of 6.9 mm **[measured]** on `full100`, so the gate sits an order of magnitude below a one row slip. |

### The decision

```
1.  Any bubble with saturation > MAX_SATURATION      -> unmeasurable, and the frame is refused (د10).
2.  max(ink) < MIN_INK                               -> the group is BLANK. Stop. (د8)
3.  every bubble ink >= MIN_INK                      -> the group is AMBIGUOUS. Stop. (د8)
4.  any bubble ink in [MIN_INK, T_MARK)              -> the group is UNCERTAIN. Stop. (rule 6)
5.  select 'one':
       rel_i = ink_i / max(ink)
       answered iff rel_top >= 0.65 and rel_second <= 0.45
       two bubbles at or above T_MARK                -> DOUBLE MARKED (reported, counted, never guessed)
       otherwise                                     -> AMBIGUOUS
6.  select 'many':
       each bubble decides alone: filled at ink >= T_MARK, empty at ink < MIN_INK, uncertain between.
       Several filled bubbles are a legitimate ANSWER, not ambiguity. (PLAN rule 2's intended exception)
7.  margin below MARGIN_FLOOR                        -> promoted to UNCERTAIN. (د13)
```

### The margin

For a group answered on bubble `t`, the margin is the smallest distance to any constraint that was actually binding, in ink units:

```
margin = min(
  ink_t - T_MARK,                        // the winner is a mark at all
  0.45 * max(ink) - ink_second,          // the runner up stays under the relative bar
  MIN_INK - min(ink)                     // at least one bubble is under the floor  (clause 3)
)
```

For a blank group, `margin = MIN_INK - max(ink)`. For an uncertain or ambiguous group, `margin = 0`, because it is already surfaced. For `select: 'many'`, the margin is the minimum of `|ink_i - T_MARK|` over the bubbles, with any bubble in the band forcing 0.

`SheetReading.quality.minMargin` is the minimum over every group, and it is a first class CI gate (Part H), because a change that keeps every decision and halves every margin is a change that will flip decisions on the next photograph taken.

## Part E: the two proven defects, fixed by construction

**Defect (a), a confident answer on an untouched question carrying 4 percent dust.**

The mechanism was `fill_i / max(fill)` with no absolute floor: on a clean row every value is comparable noise, so the second exceeds 0.45 and the question is reported ambiguous (interrupting the teacher five times for a student who skipped five questions); and on a row carrying one dust speck three times its neighbours, the ratio is 1.00 and the second is 0.33, so **a confident wrong letter is issued**.

It is fixed by ordering, not by a better denominator: **step 2 of the decision runs before any ratio exists.** `max(ink) < 0.25` returns `BLANK` and stops, and 0.25 is measured on the `K` to `W` scale that the sheet's own printed furniture declares, which is what makes an absolute number safe under a shadow. Dust at 4 percent coverage of the disc contributes ink of roughly 0.03, which is a fifth of the trace threshold and an eighth of the floor.

Three structural properties make this unrepairable-into-a-bug rather than merely fixed today:

1. `ink` is the argument to the floor, and `ink` is computed in `measure/photometry.ts` which has no access to any group's contents. **The denominator can never be made of the thing being measured**, because the denominator is `W * (1 - k)` and both come from printed furniture.
2. The relative rule is unreachable from a blank group: `decide/group.ts` returns before computing `rel_i`, and the `switch` over the verdict union is exhaustive with no `default`, so adding a state breaks the build rather than falling through.
3. **No page wide or group wide order statistic is permitted to divide.** A per sheet term may only ever be additive and bounded, never a divisor, and never an order statistic over the same bubbles whose verdicts it decides. This rule exists because the most attractive wrong fix, normalising against a page quantile pair, is the same defect at page scope and fires on a sparsely answered paper.

**Defect (b), the printed code at 0.64 px per module after `resize x0.25`.**

Fixed by decision 8 and by there being no other resolution to measure from. Decimation exists only to find the sheet; there is no warp, so there is no reduced raster the code could accidentally be read from. The code is sampled through the projector at the frame's native resolution, and two gates make the failure named rather than silent: the page gate at 6 px/mm and the **pre decode** code gate at 3 px per module, which emits `resolution_low { need: 'code' }` and the instruction "come closer" (د11's message) before a single module is sampled.

**[computed]** At the mandated 1440p over 210 mm the module is 3.43 px; at 1080p it is 2.57 px and the frame is refused with a reason a teacher can act on, which is 4ب-1's third complaint (the highest traffic support topic in the category) answered directly rather than with a sharpness slider.

## Part F: determinism, and how it is tested

Three properties, kept separate because conflating them is what produced the competitor's two scores in two minutes (note 49).

**1. Engine determinism: the same bytes give the same bits on Hermes and V8.** Decision 16, enforced by `test/purity.test.ts`.

**2. Geometric determinism: the estimator integrates the same physical points.** Decision 2. The lattices are in units of `r` in page millimetres, so two photographs at different distances sample the same graphite and differ only in the pixel values there. No resampling stage sits between the sensor and the decision.

**3. Decision determinism: what can actually be promised across two photographs.** Identical ink values from two photographs are physically impossible. The guarantee is instead that **nothing close enough to flip is ever silently decided**, carried by the margin floor of Part D, and it is verified rather than asserted by the perturbation set of decision 10.

**The tests.**

| Test | Asserts |
|---|---|
| `purity.test.ts` | No banned identifier anywhere in `src/`. Currently fails on 16 call sites in the working tree prototype. |
| `determinism.test.ts` | The same input scanned twice deep-equals. Trivially true, kept because a cache or a `Date.now()` would break it. |
| `dither.test.ts` | A **deterministic ±1 grey dither keyed off pixel coordinates** (checkerboard, no RNG) changes no verdict except toward uncertain. A uniform ±1 shift is a tautology here (`ink` is a ratio of differences and is unchanged by construction), so it must be spatially varying to test anything. |
| `perturbation.test.ts` | The full 81 member CI set of decision 10 over every synthetic and golden paper produces a byte identical **complete result**: `answers`, blank set, ambiguous set, uncertain bubble set, glare tags, escape tags, id status, key version status. That list is criterion 12 verbatim, and `readingDigest` covers exactly it. |
| `agree.test.ts` | Three identical frames from a static pose do **not** satisfy `agree()`. This is the test that PLAN rule 3 as written would have failed. |
